model_leak_root_cause.symptom: Repeated EXIT=124 timeouts and a 30-second latency stall in a worker call. Looked like a flaky suite.
model_leak_root_cause.actual_cause: Ollama keeps models RESIDENT in RAM until they expire or are explicitly unloaded. My team runs never released them, so llama-server processes accumulated to ~1.3 GB on a 16 GB host (81% used, 3.3 GB free).
model_leak_root_cause.not_oom: Checked the Windows event log: no recent OOM events (last was 24 Sept, two weeks earlier). This was resource starvation degrading performance, not an OS kill.
model_leak_root_cause.evidence: One worker call took 30037.91 ms where normal calls take ~2 s, then failed UNKNOWN_PROVIDER_ERROR. Ollama answered /api/tags in 1.2-1.6 s when probed separately, proving the runtime was healthy and the stall was local contention.
model_leak_root_cause.fix: release_models() unloads every model a run loaded; called on run_bounded_team_task, run_parallel_branches, run_solo_baseline and compare_solo_vs_team (the last two in finally blocks so a failure cannot strand a model).
model_leak_root_cause.recovered: Unloaded a stale 1.09 GB server by hand -> 4.46 GB free (73.9%). Only Hermes' own llama-server (PID 2072) was left untouched, as it is not ours to manage.
model_leak_root_cause.result: Full team suite 37/37 pass in 288.87 s with 0 skips - the first complete clean run of the file.
